result:
Created two self-contained JUnit 5 test classes:

- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DurationUtilsAgentTest.java` — covers `accept` (normal, null consumer, null duration), `get`/`getMillis`/`getSeconds` defaulting, `getNanosOfMilli`/deprecated `getNanosOfMiili`, `isPositive` (positive/zero/negative), `of(FailableRunnable/FailableConsumer)` including exception propagation, `since`, `toDuration`, `toChronoUnit` (all enum values + null), `toMillisInt` (normal, overflow clamping to `MAX_VALUE`/`MIN_VALUE`, null → NPE), `zeroIfNull`, and the deprecated default constructor.
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/StopWatchAgentTest.java` — covers lifecycle state transitions (`start`/`stop`/`suspend`/`resume`/`split`/`unsplit`/`reset`) and their illegal-state error cases, timing accessors (`getNanoTime`, `getTime`, `getDuration`, `getTime(TimeUnit)`), split list immutability, `Split` accessors, start/stop instants (including deprecated millis accessors), `toString`/`toSplitString`/`formatTime`/`formatSplitTime` with and without a message, and the `get`/`run`/`getT`/`runT` helper methods including exception propagation and suspend-after-call behavior.

Both were adjusted to match actual `StopWatch.split()` semantics (calling it twice is allowed and simply records two splits, since `split()` doesn't change `runningState`). All 74 tests pass via `./_tools/test.sh`.
